title: Private-address block checks only the literal hostname; DNS names, redirects and bracketed IPv6 bypass it
reason: The check runs on the URL's hostname string only: a domain that resolves to 127.0.0.1/169.254.169.254 (e.g. a wildcard DNS name or 'localhost.'), a public URL that 302-redirects to an internal address (fetch follows redirects by default), or a bracketed IPv6 host such as http://[::1]/ all pass, so a prompt-injected fetch reaches localhost services or cloud metadata and the response is returned to the model.
fix: Resolve the hostname (dns.lookup all addresses), reject loopback/private/link-local/unique-local/IPv4-mapped ranges on the resolved IPs and connect to the checked IP (custom undici dispatcher/lookup), set redirect: 'manual' and re-validate each Location hop, and strip brackets before checking IPv6.

title: Fetched web content returned unmarked into the model context

evidence.quote: return { content: [{ type: "text", text: html }], isError: false };
return { content: [{ type: "text", text: markdown }], isError: false };

reason: Arbitrary web pages are returned verbatim as tool output with nothing marking them as untrusted data; this is the main path by which injected instructions reach an agent, and the same tools (any URL, caller-set headers) give that agent a way to send data out in the query string.
fix: Wrap results in a clearly delimited untrusted-content block and tell the host to require approval for follow-up actions; consider a domain allowlist option.

title: Whole response body is downloaded before max_length is applied
reason: max_length only truncates after the full body is read into memory (and parsed by JSDOM for fetch_txt), and there is no request timeout, so a huge or never-ending response can exhaust memory or hang the server.
fix: Stream the body and stop after a byte cap (e.g. 5 MB), and pass an AbortSignal.timeout() to fetch.
